content.text: Now I'll add request logging using Next.js middleware, which is the best approach to log all requests to the console.

Perfect! I've added request logging to your Next.js app by creating a `middleware.ts` file at the root of your project.

This middleware will log every request to the console with:
- Timestamp (ISO format)
- HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
- Full URL
- User-Agent header

The logs will appear in your terminal when you run the dev server. For example:
```
[2026-02-10T12:34:56.789Z] GET http://localhost:3000/ - User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0...
```

The middleware is configured to match all routes except Next.js internal routes like static files, image optimization, and favicon, so you'll only see actual page requests.
